title: Pot-roast Beef Brisket with Hasselback Carrots
description: Rolled beef brisket slow-cooked in a herby stock gravy until fall-apart tender, served with roasted hasselback carrots.
ingredients: 8 similar-sized carrots, peeled but left whole
steps: Sear beef in cooking spray over high heat for 1 minute each side; transfer to casserole dish.
Stir-fry onions, garlic and celery in same pan for 5 minutes; transfer to casserole.

Mix stock with mustard powder, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, rosemary and tomato purée. Mix cornflour with 1 tbsp cold water; stir into stock. Pour over beef; season; lid on; cook 4 hours, turning meat halfway.
With ~1 hour left, boil carrots whole for 10 minutes; drain; cool under running water.
Place each carrot between 2 wooden spoon handles; slice evenly across at ~5mm intervals to create hasselback effect.
Place carrots on baking tray; spray; season; roast at 200°C for 40 minutes until browned.
Remove beef; blend remaining pan contents with hand blender to make gravy.
Slice or pull apart beef with 2 forks; serve with gravy and hasselback carrots.
notes: Always rest a roast chicken or beef for at least 15 minutes after cooking. Make stock with leftovers (see p.217).
source: The Slimming Foodie by Pip Payne (2021)
